# niksi

> `nik` installs agent skills from Git repositories and local directories. It
> scans every file before it writes, records each skill in `niksi-lock.json`,
> and links it into Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and other agents.

The binary is `nik`. `npx niksi` runs it without installing. An agent's shell
has no terminal, so pass every answer as a flag, and leave critical findings
for the user to approve in their own terminal. The niksi skill teaches an
agent this workflow.

## Docs

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/osrim/niksi/main/README.md): what niksi does, how to install it, and a quick start
- [Commands](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/osrim/niksi/main/docs/commands.md): every command, flag, and exit code, plus non-interactive use and `nik list --json`
- [Configuration](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/osrim/niksi/main/docs/configuration.md): scope, agents, paths, environment variables, and the project's `niksi.json`
- [Lockfile format](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/osrim/niksi/main/docs/lockfile.md): every field of `niksi-lock.json` and how the integrity is computed
- [Security scan](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/osrim/niksi/main/docs/security-scan.md): what the scan catches, its severities, and what it cannot catch
- [CI](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/osrim/niksi/main/docs/ci.md): the GitHub Action and its modes

## Agent skill

- [niksi skill](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/osrim/niksi/main/skills/niksi/SKILL.md): install, update, and read installed skills with `nik` from an agent's shell
